name: claudeblender
description: A pane with a live low-res view of your Blender scene, redrawn in half-block pixels after every Blender edit Claude or a subagent makes, with an animation preview, motion effects and settings in /config

autoOpen.title: Open on the first edit
autoOpen.description: on: the pane opens by itself the first time Claude or a subagent edits the Blender scene in a session (an unasked pane shows from 144 terminal columns, 110 once you have opened it yourself). Closing it by hand keeps it closed for the rest of the session; /blender opens it again. off: only /blender opens it.

view.title: View
view.description: The view the pane starts each session with; the chips under the picture change it for the session. viewport: what the largest 3D Viewport in Blender shows, at its shape. camera: through the scene camera, at the render resolution's shape. top, bottom, front, back, left, right: straight-on orthographic views framed on the scene, like Blender's numpad views. iso: a three-quarter view from the front right, above. Your own viewport and active camera never move.

shading.title: Shading
shading.description: solid: Blender's Solid shading, fast and clear. material: Material Preview, the scene's real material colors; slower, and the first draw after new materials may show them unfinished. The viewport's own shading is put back after each draw.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: How the pane moves. lively: a new frame wipes in behind a warm glint line, from the top and from the left by turns, the held frame gently brightens and darkens while Blender draws, the dot spins ◐ ◓ ◑ ◒ every 0.2 s, the object count and draw time roll with the changed digits flashing, the name of the agent that made the edit pulses in its color, ✦ fresh twinkles for 2 s, and a failed draw pulses ✗ red. subtle: the wipe without the glint, a fainter glow, the spinner a step every second, softer pulses, a plain fresh. off: a still pane, each frame swapped in at once.

redraw.title: Redraw on
redraw.description: edits: an execute_blender_code call that only reads the scene (no bpy.ops, no assignment to an object's property, no call that can write) draws nothing; when in doubt it draws. every: every execute_blender_code call draws, as import_asset and generate_3d always do.

server.title: Blender MCP server
server.description: The name of the Blender MCP server as /mcp lists it.
